pages.text: "Time to eat!" Nils the little bear came from digging in the garden. His dirty paws grabbed steaming bread. Grandpa Bruno asked, "What about your paws?" Nils pretended not to hear and ate.
"I can go to the tub later! Tummy first!" Nils gripped the bread hard. Dirt followed his pawprints onto it. Brown marks dotted it; soil grains fell.
A little later, his tummy grumbled and grumbled. "It hurts..." Nils curled beside the table, rubbing his belly with both paws. Grandpa adjusted his glasses and bent his knees. "Let's see. Tears too."
Grandpa held up Nils's paw between them. "Things you can't see cling to dirt. They got on the bread and into your tummy." His eyes widened. "Will it keep hurting?" "Don't worry. To the water tub."
"Three washing steps! One—dip into water!" Grandpa said by the well's tub. Nils dipped both paws. Dirt loosened, turning the water brown. "Wow! Dirt went into the water!"
"Two—rub paws together!" Nils rubbed both paws. Backs too, right up to the wrists. Grandpa sang, "Scrub, scrub—goodbye, dirt!"
"Three—rinse with fresh water!" Grandpa opened the well lid, drew new water, and poured. Brown water ran off. "Scrub, scrub—goodbye, dirt! Goodbye, wigglers!" Nils shook his paws.
His paws were fresh, not a strand of fur clumped. Drops fell from the tips. "Leaving dirt at the tub means my tummy doesn't hurt!" Nils smiled wide.
The next day, Nils went to the tub before bread. "Paws first!" One, dip. Two, rub. Three, rinse with fresh water and shake! Both paws high above his head. "Scrub, scrub—goodbye, dirt!"
Grandpa hugged him from behind. "Paws like new!" Leave dirt at the tub, and bread tastes better. Nils took bread with clean paws. "Scrub, scrub—goodbye, dirt! Yum!"
